published_description: A bacterial Isc mechanism for iron-sulfur cluster assembly and transfer supported by Isc ferredoxin and the dedicated HscBA cycle. IscS mobilizes cysteine sulfur as a persulfide and supplies IscU, the transient cluster scaffold. Reduced Isc ferredoxin supplies reducing equivalents; HscB recruits IscU to the HscA ATPase, coupling ATP hydrolysis to cluster release and delivery. An optional IscA carrier branch supports condition- and client-dependent iron or cluster handling. Reduced anaerobic ISC implementations and scaffold-suppressor bypasses have different component requirements. IscR regulation, CyaY and IscX modulation, upstream iron and reductant supply, mitochondrial ISC, and the separate Suf and Nif systems lie outside this mechanism.
